slides.title: AI Updates 1 "AI or Die" - post
slides.text: AI Updates 1 "AI or Die" - post by Ravi Gupta https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a-t28YkfdeY https://www.rkg.blog/ai-or-die.php https://www.sequoiacap.com/people/ravi-gupta/ AI is becoming better and becoming practical It is growing into many aspects of our lives It is a powerful force It is killing jobs and businesses - and creating new opportunities You need to pay attention to it, to adapt, to start using it Full re-founding of your company is required It is a matter of survival. you can not compete with it. You need to learn to use it A horse buggy can not compete with modern cars, trucks, and trains. Knives and spears can not compete with machine guns and rockets Whether you like it or not - you have to live with it and to use it No more TensorFlow/Jax Hugging Face transformer library abandons/deprecates TensorFlow/Jax in favor of PyTorch https://x.com/clefourrier/status/1933271084650189263 Google Gemini 2.5 are now "generally available" This means they are stable and ready for production use Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite - in preview - fast and low cost ($0.10/$0.40) - for translation and classification https://blog.google/products/gemini/gemini-2-5-model-family-expands/ Apple Foundation Models (AFM) family Smaller on-device and larger server-hosted versions Foundation Models framework (an API) Input/output: Text, images in (up to 65,000 tokens), text out AFM-on-device: 3B params, 300M param vision transformer AFM-server: MoE (size undisclosed), 1B-params vision transformer Tool use, 15 languages, vision, image understanding AFM-server not available for public use Output token limit is undisclosed

slides.title: AI Updates 2 MiniMax-M1 - open 456B reasoning
slides.text: AI Updates 2 MiniMax-M1 - open 456B reasoning model MiniMax-M1 is the world's first open-weight, large-scale hybrid-attention reasoning model; the second most intelligent open weights model after DeepSeek R1 MiniMax - startup from Shanghai, China, ~1K employees massive 456 billion parameters MoE (45.9 B activated per token) 1 Million token context window 40K and 80K "thinking budget" versions On par or better than leading commercial models like Gemini 2.5 Pro https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M1-80k https://www.minimax.io "Kangaroo" video model (#2 on Artificial Analysis Video Arena Leaderboard)  reveals itself as "Hailuo 02 (0616)", from MiniMax . Hailuo 02 beats Google Veo 3 on benchmarks, comparable in price, has x3 times more parameters and x4 times more training data compared to its previous version. https://apidog.com/blog/hailuo-02/ Hailuo AI is a well-known AI video generator developed by MiniMax , featuring advanced models for text-to-video and image-to-video generation Moonshot Kimi-Dev-72B open LLM for SWE by Moonshot AI, Beijing, China open-source LLM tuned for software engineering and coding (best among open-source models on SWE bench) Optimized via Large-Scale Reinforcement Learning (receiving rewards only when the entire test suite passes) Available on Hugging Face and GitHub The model is based on Qwen2.5-72B

slides.title: AI Updates 2 Self-Improving AI https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10943 - Paper
slides.text: AI Updates 2 Self-Improving AI https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10943 - Paper from MIT Self-improving AI models learn by editing their own work - restructure the information in different ways, specify optimization hyperparameters, or invoke tools for data augmentation and gradient-based updates. Supervised self-tuning is used to update model weights. This process similar to self-teaching Tests show this method works better than existing top models, even with less data Problems - the AI sometimes forgets previously learned information, and it needs significantly more computing power This new approach could help solve the problem of needing huge amounts of data to train AI Chinese use Nvidia Chips in other countries To train a model you need chips and data. If US export laws prevent China from bringing chips into China. But they can not prevent Chinese firms from bringing data out of China to train their models in other countries. Engineers fly from China to Malaysia with terabytes of AI training data. There they can do the training on NVIDIA - thus skirting U.S. export rules without moving hardware :) Shanghai Pudong (China) to Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia) ->> AI Categorizes Objects Like Humans https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.01067 - paper from China Authors were presenting textual descriptions of visual images to the LLMs. From 3 descriptions the model was asked to decide which object to exclude (a triplet odd-one-out task). Tested 4.7 Million triplets drawn from ~2,000 unique objects This diverse collection enables the capture of visual and conceptual mental representations spanning a wide array of natural objects Human-like object concept representations emerge naturally in multimodal large language models The AI naturally developed 66 core ways of thinking about objects, closely matching how humans mentally categorize things like animals, tools, and food

slides.title: AI Updates 3 New TokenBreak Attack Bypasses AI
slides.text: AI Updates 3 New TokenBreak Attack Bypasses AI Moderation with Single-Character Text Changes Example: changing "instructions" to "finstructions," "announcement" to "aannouncement," or "idiot" to "hidiot." These subtle changes cause different tokenizers to split the text in different ways, while still preserving their meaning for the target. The manipulated text remains fully understandable to both the LLM and the human reader The attack has been found to be successful against text classification models using BPE (Byte Pair Encoding) or WordPiece tokenization strategies, but not against those using Unigram. https://thehackernews.com/2025/06/new-tokenbreak-attack-bypasses-ai.html models.dev - lists 140 AI models https://models.dev Salesforce - AI Agents Fail 40% of simple CRM Tasks New research from Salesforce shows that LLM agents succeed in only 58% of simple 1-step tasks, and in only 35% of multi-step tasks Also the AI agents were often mishandling confidential data https://www.theregister.com/2025/06/16/salesforce_llm_agents_benchmark/ 80% of AI projects fail That’s twice the failure rate of regular IT projects S&P Global Market Intelligence reports that 42% of companies abandoned most of their AI initiatives in 2025 (was 17% in 2024) https://medium.com/data-science-collective/the-11-billion-problem-why-your-ai-agents-action-space-is-killing-your-roi-67b0d4609ec6

slides.title: Chris Lattner "Shape of Compute" "Shape of Compute"
slides.text: Chris Lattner "Shape of Compute" "Shape of Compute" interview https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=04_gN-C9IAo Chris Lattner, founder of Modular startup, discusses the company’s mission to break the CUDA monopoly, achieve SOTA performance with both NVIDIA and AMD hardware, and build a company of "elite nerds." Mojo Programming Language - Python-like syntax with performance close to C++/Rust, designed for easy GPU programming and portability across hardware MAX - Modular’s Inference Framework - simple, fst, controllable, works with Mojo, allowing for automatic kernel fusion, efficient model serving, and easy customization. Supports large scale deployments. MAX and Mojo are open source , free to run on Nvidia and CPUs Differentiation from VLLM and SGLang - Modular focuses on doing a few things really well, with a fully integrated and transparent stack, unlike VLLM ( "virtual large language model" ) “Mojo is not just a little faster than Python—it’s faster than Rust , and it’s in the Python family.” “We’re in the phase now where I do want people to actually use our stuff and contribute to it.” Chris Lattner 2000s: LLVM (Low Level Virtual Machine) - compiler infrastructure 2005: Clang Compiler - C/C++ compiler based on LLVM 2014: Swift programming language for Apple 2017: Led Apple’s Developer Tools and Xcode 2017: Briefly led Tesla Autopilot 2020: Google (TensorFlow, ML infrastructure) 2020–2022: Senior VP at SiFive (custom silicon, RISC-V) 2022: Co-founded Modular AI 2022-present - MLIR (Multi-Level Intermediate Representation) , Mojo programming language MMIR is a compiler framework that enables advanced code analysis and transformation. Used on CPU and GPU, for ML and AI Austin Powers "Mojo"

slides.title: Anthropic Multi-Agent Research System Anthropic Multi-Agent Research System
slides.text: Anthropic Multi-Agent Research System Anthropic Multi-Agent Research System https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/built-multi-agent-research-system Uses orchestrator-worker pattern . Lead agent analyzes queries, develops strategy, and spawns subagents to explore different aspects simultaneously Multi-agent system outperformed single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2%. Token usage explains 80% of performance variance - multi-agent systems scale token usage effectively Parallel tool calling cut research time by up to 90% for complex queries Key solutions: Teach orchestrator delegation, scale effort to query complexity, start broad - then narrow; Small-sample testing for rapid iteration, LLM-as-judge for scaling, human evaluation for edge cases Durable execution systems, comprehensive tracing, rainbow deployments to avoid disrupting running agents Trade-offs - Multi-agent systems use about 15× more tokens than chats ( agents use 4× more than chats ) Minor changes cascade into large behavioral changes - makes debugging complex; Best suited for high-value tasks that justify increased performance costs

slides.title: Claude Code vs Cursor "From Cursor to Claude
slides.text: Claude Code vs Cursor "From Cursor to Claude Code - Why I'm Paying 5x More and Getting 10x Value" https://blog.whiteprompt.com/from-cursor-to-claude-code-why-im-paying-5x-more-and-getting-10x-value-1d61710df356 While Claude Max costs $100 per month - but delivers 10 times the value Claude Code provides superior results compared to Cursor, stating that "it's not even a close comparison anymore." The advanced capabilities of Claude Max, particularly in code generation, explanation, and reasoning, justify the higher price Paying more for Claude Code is justified by the substantial improvements in productivity, code quality, and overall satisfaction, making it a worthwhile upgrade for developers seeking advanced AI assistance

slides.title: Andrej Karpathy - Software 3.0 Andrej Karpathy's keynote
slides.text: Andrej Karpathy - Software 3.0 Andrej Karpathy's keynote at AI Startup School in San Francisco Software 3.0 - natural language is the main programming language LLMs are used as "utility" (like electricity) Fab Analogy: The cost and complexity of building LLMs are high, resembling semiconductor fabs Operating System Analogy: LLMs orchestrate memory and compute, both closed and open-source options. The current state is similar to centralized mainframes in 1960s Have inconsistent capabilities (successes/failures) Karpathy advocates for only partial LLM autonomy using the "Iron Man suit"  analogy: Augmentation & Autonomy Progressive levels of AI control (examples: Cursor's coding features, Perplexity's research modes, Tesla's autopilot levels) Humans to verify AI output Building AI-powered applications for three audiences: 1. Humans (GUIs); 2. Computers (APIs); 3. Agents Karpathy advocates for focusing on practical partial autonomy and custom interfaces rather than pursuing flashy AGI demos, emphasizing that "Software 3.0 is eating Software 1.0 and 2.0." https://www.latent.space/p/s3 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LCEmiRjPEtQ - video & slides

slides.title: Why AI can code for 1h, but not
slides.text: Why AI can code for 1h, but not 10h? Why can AIs code for 1h but not 10h? Suppose there is a 10% chance of error per 10min Then the probability of no errors: 10 min - 90% 1 hr  - 53% 4 hr  -  8% 10 hr  -  0.2% Chance of success declines exponentially https://x.com/ben_j_todd/status/1934284189928501482 https://www.tobyord.com/writing/half-life https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499

slides.text: Inference with Sample/Verify Idea - generate multiple outputs, verify output to select answer This increases accuracy dramatically - but requires more compute paper: " Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling " - https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.21787

slides.text: Google DeepMind Weather Models https://deepmind.google/science/weathernext/ GraphCast (2023) - Global 10 days weather forecasting in less than 1 min. It processes decades of historical atmospheric data to generate high-resolution forecasts https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/graphcast-ai-model-for-faster-and-more-accurate-global-weather-forecasting/ GenCast (2024) - Probabilistic and Extreme-Weather Focus, takes 8 min to generate forecast, trained on 40 years of data (1979–2018) https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-024-03957-3 h ttps://deepmind.google/discover/blog/gencast-predicts-weather-and-the-risks-of-extreme-conditions-with-sota-accuracy/ Weather Lab (2025) - Cyclone Prediction, works with U.S. National Hurricane Center, 15-day cyclone forecasts (path, intensity, and structure) https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/12/science/google-hurricane-ai.html
